BRIEF: verify FACTS, not prose — re-run the document's own commands against the repository and report any figure that does not reproduce; adjudicate whether the recommendation is supported; check every item in the document's 'What is not true' section, on the grounds that a false entry there is worse than an omission because readers trust it most; and specifically check whether the author's decision NOT to file a stale-lease defect had suppressed a real finding. The reviewer recomputed the frozen manifest by taking all 138 SHA-256 values from `git show v5.0.0:<path>` rather than invoking `make verify-release`, to honour the read-only constraint while still checking the claim. findings.evidence: `gh run view 36232214628 --log | grep -oE 'Assertions executed: [0-9]+' | tail -1` returns 7764. The same command against run 36228388997 (commit 44a1777) returns 7746. Verified independently by the document's author after the finding was raised.
findings.description: The L1 assertion count quoted for run 36232214628 is 7,746. The actual value is 7,764; 7,746 belongs to a different run at a different commit. Two errors compounded — a digit transposition and attribution to the wrong run. FIX: correct to 7,764 and extract the value from the cited run.

findings.evidence: Run 36232214628's L2 job reports `Specs:      Total: 48  Passed: 32  Failed: 1  Skipped: 15  Partial: 4` with 2,353 passing assertions. Confirmed by the author against the same log.
findings.description: FALSE STATEMENT INSIDE THE SECTION LISTING FALSE STATEMENTS. The document asserts that at HEAD 'every L2 spec skips on BD_SHIM_ONLY=1' and that L2 therefore gives 'near-zero signal'. In fact 32 of 48 specs pass and 15 skip. The error came from generalising a log excerpt showing consecutive skips into a universal, without counting. This is the worst placement for a false claim because readers trust that section most. FIX: state the measured L2 result and identify which 15 specs skip.

findings.evidence: The published priority table sums 4 + 90 + 105 + 96 + 14 = 309, against a stated total of 292. `bd list` defaults to `--limit 50` and the verification command in section 21 omits `--limit 0`, so the query was not exhaustive.
findings.description: The backlog figures are internally inconsistent and were not exhaustively measured. Section 9 presents 292 as an OPEN count; section 16 reuses the same number as a LIVE TOTAL — different populations. Every backlog figure in the document should be treated as unverified pending an exhaustive, status-scoped re-measurement. The four P0 identities are unaffected, having been read individually. FIX: re-measure with an exhaustive query, define the included statuses, and compare ledger and live store over the same population.

findings.evidence: The 442 rows of .beads/issues.jsonl span all statuses (208 open, 10 in_progress, 1 deferred, 223 closed). The 292 figure was measured with `--status open`.
findings.description: The item asserts that '292 open tasks is the backlog' is false, and offers 442 ledger rows as the evidence. The two counts cover different populations and the comparison cannot support the claim. The defensible proposition is narrower and survives: .beads/issues.jsonl (mtime Aug 26) is not a current reflection of the live store and must not be read as ground truth. FIX: state the proposition the evidence actually supports, and verify it with status-scoped counts on both sides.

findings.evidence: `grep -c 'test-cmd' manifests/v5.0.0.sha256` -> 0; `grep -c '\.claude/scripts/tests/' manifests/v5.0.0.sha256` -> 0; `grep -c 'impact-report.test.sh' manifests/v5.0.0.sha256` -> 0. Run by the author after the finding was raised, all three confirming.
findings.description: THE CONSUMER-EXPOSURE ARGUMENT IS FALSE, AND IT OVERSTATED THE COST OF RELEASING. Section 19 argues that teammates installing from main would receive `.claude/test-cmd` narrowing their own Stop gate, and would run the kyj5 litter-producing L1 test. Neither reaches a target: `.claude/test-cmd` is untracked and absent from the shipped manifest, `.claude/scripts/tests/` is repository-only, and impact-report.test.sh is not installed. FIX: describe both as repository-maintainer hygiene defects rather than installed-user exposure. The recommendation direction survives, but two of the three urgency reasons given were wrong about who is affected.

Absence of evidence in an audit that explicitly declined to perform the install check does not establish falsity. A reader cannot reproduce the document from it alone, which is a defect in the artifact's central promise — a verification section that does not verify is the same family the whole arc is about.
